findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) on duty at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The owner who is a CFPM arrived during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a CFPM with their Allergen training on duty during all hours of operation and food preparation. It is recommended to have multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: There were no signed employee reporting agreements available during the inspection. A follow up is scheduled for 6/15/2026 to ensure that there are signed employee reporting agreements available for every employee. Ensure that there are signed employee reporting agreements available for every employee and that there is a person in charge that is knowledgeable on where they are in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: There was not a Norovirus cleanup policy available in the facility. CORRECTED- A Norovirus cleanup policy was provided and the facility possesses bleach to effectively complete the procedure. Ensure that there is always a vomit/diarrhea clean-up policy available in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There was observed to be ice in the server station handwashing sink, indicating that a drink had been dumped in the sink. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that staff are educated that handwashing sinks should only be used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was observed to be raw pork over ready-to-eat food items in the bottom of the preparation cooler along the cook-line. CORRECTED- An employee switched the pork to be below the ready-to-eat food items. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The ice scoop for the ice machine was observed to be stored on a soda syrup box. CORRECTED- This was discussed with an employee, who switched the scoop to be in a pan. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are being stored on a clean, sanitized surface.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket in the kitchen that is used by the servers was observed to bleach out the Chlorine test strip, indicating that it is at a disinfectant level and is toxic to use on food-contact surfaces. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was re-made and tested to be at 200ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that staff are educated on how to properly make a sanitizer bucket to make sure that it is at a label-recommended concentration that is safe to use on food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 7-202.12(A) Conditions of Use. POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS shall be: (A) Used according to: (1) LAW and this Code, (2) Manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions that state that use is allowed in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, (3) The conditions of certification, if certification is required, for use of the pest control materials, and (4) Additional conditions that may be established by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: The bowls next to the soup hot holding were observed to be stored with their food-contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that single-service articles and utensils, including bowls that are going to be used once for a customer and then warewashed, are handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent contamination to food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The floor under the fryers is observed to have an accumulation of food debris and soil residue on it. Ensure that these floors are cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) on duty at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The owner who is a CFPM arrived during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on duty during all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to go outside with gloves on and then return to the cook-line and continue food preparation. CORRECTED- The employee was educated that when engaging in tasks that contaminate gloves, handwashing and changing gloves needs to occur. The employee then proceeded to rinse their hands, without soap, in a non-handwashing sink. The employee was educated on this as well and washed their hands in the handwashing sink. Ensure that food employees are educated on when to wash their hands and change their gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to go outside with gloves on and then return to the cook-line and continue food preparation. The employee was educated that when engaging in tasks that contaminate gloves, handwashing and changing gloves needs to occur. The employee then proceeded to rinse their hands, without soap, in a non-handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The employee was educated on this as well and washed their hands in the handwashing sink. Ensure that all employees are educated that handwashing should only be done in a handwashing sink.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The soap dispenser in the women’s bathroom was observed to not be functional and there was no soap at the handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The PIC obtained batteries for the soap dispenser and fixed it during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap at every handwashing sink.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Two improper storage orders were observed in the following area:
- Raw chicken wings stored above lemons and other cooked meats inside of the standing cooler (near the back door)
- Raw chicken stored above diced tomatoes and several rolls of raw beef.

Discussed with the person-in-charge that raw chicken has the highest internal cooking temperature of 165F and must always be stored at the bottom shelf of cold holding units. The items were rearranged to correct the violation. Ensure that ready-to-eat RTE foods and ground beef are stored above all raw chicken products to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The employee washing dishes was observed to wash and rinse the dishes, then place them on the clean dish rack without sanitizing. CORRECTED- The employee was educated that after being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils need to be sanitized either manually or through mechanical operations. The triple sink is observed to not have any stoppers that would allow for proper sanitizing in this manner. Stoppers are important to have in case the dish machine is not properly sanitizing. This was discussed with the PIC. The dish machine is properly chemical sanitizing with Chlorine sanitizer and the employee stated that they will be using that for cleaning dishes instead of using the triple sink. Ensure that equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils are being sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(1) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (1) Except as specified under Subparagraph (C)(2) of this section, a contact time of at least 10 seconds for a chlorine solution specified under 4-501.114(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The Chlorine sanitizer bucket on the cook-line was observed to be at 0ppm. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at 150ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are frequently tested and remade if not at a label-recommended concentration. Sanitizer buckets should typically be changed every two to four hours, or sooner if the bucket is heavily used.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The cheese sauce on the steam table was observed to only be at 129F. CORRECTED- An employee reheated the cheese sauce on the stove and the cheese sauce probed to be at 166F. Ensure that Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are being held at 135F or above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were two containers of cooked potatoes that were observed to be cooling within the double-door standing cooler. The potatoes were covered in plastic wrap and probed to be at 67F. The potatoes were date-marked that they had been cooked on 2/25 (today’s date), but the employee was unsure of the exact time the potatoes had been cooked. CORRECTED- The plastic wrap was removed from the top of the potatoes and the potatoes were placed in a standing freezer to allow for more rapid cooling. The potatoes probed to be at 47F at the end of the inspection. The employee was educated that when foods are being cooled, they should be uncovered and there should be less in the pan to allow for more rapid cooling. The potatoes were observed to be mounded in the pan and the employee stated they will place less in the pan going forward. Cooling of foods should be monitored. Foods need to be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours, and then from 70F to under 41F within another four hours, for a total of six hours for cooling.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: There was not a probe thermometer observed within the facility. A follow up is scheduled for 3/6/2026 to ensure that a probe thermometer is available and easily accessible in the facility. There should always be a probe thermometer in the facility to allow for measuring the temperature of foods being cooked, cooled, or reheated.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
There was observed to be mashed potatoes in a sour cream container in the bottom of a prep cooler in the kitchen. The facility is observed to be re-using plastic single-use containers for food storage, such as sour cream containers. Food-contact surfaces should be durable, corrosion-resistant, and about to withstand repeated warewashing. Cease re-using these containers for food storage (unless the foods are individually packaged, such as the containers of condiments in the bottom of the server preparation cooler that are being stored in a sour cream container) and obtain containers that are meant to be re-used. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: A pot of potatoes was stored on a crate directly underneath the handwashing sink in the kitchen area. Shown to PIC and the potatoes were moved. Food shall never be stored on the floor or in a manner where they are exposed to contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Cooked breakfast sausages stored on the kitchen’s steam table were probed at 72F. PIC mentioned that the sausages were cooked earlier in the morning around 6am. Discussed the need to either keep the sausages hot held or on time control. PIC will use the steam table from now on to maintain the safety of the food. The sausages were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS (time/temperature control) foods are held at 135F or above to maintain proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility has mostly date marked TCS foods that are stored in house longer than 24 hours, however, a few food items lacked date marking in coolers throughout the facility. Sliced meats, cooked meats, and sauces stored in the back coolers and in the prep coolers along the cook-line were observed without date marking. Ensure that TCS foods stored in house overnight are date marked and used with 7 days of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: A container of the gravy was observed on the counter at room temperature. PIC mentioned that gravy was cooked earlier in the morning and was placed on the counter to cool. Discussed proper cooling procedures for TCS food items. The gravy was placed into the back standing cooler to finish the cooling process. Be sure that TCS foods are never cooled at room temperature. Instead, place food in cold holding equipment, on ice, or any other effective method of cooling to ensure safety of food.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the facility hot holding various food items in plastic containers on the hot line such as cheese sauces, gravies, and other sauces. Discussed with PIC that the containers are not approved to hold hot foods, nor are they sufficient enough to withstand repeat ware-washings. Instructed the facility to use stainless steel containers to hold hot foods. Ensure that materials used for hot holding are food safety approved, durable, and long lasting. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer bucket available along the kitchen’s cook-line. A sanitizer solution was prepared and tested at 100ppm (CL) to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are available in all areas where food prep occurs, including the cook-line and the service station.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: A pot of cooked potatoes was observed stored on the floor near the triple sink and next to a shelf that stores chemicals. Discussed with the PIC and the pot of potatoes were moved to a countertop. Food shall never be stored on the floor or near chemicals. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
findings.comment: Potatoes stored in a pot on the floor were probed at 70F. The potatoes had been recently cooked and were in the process of cooling. The potatoes were placed in the cooler to finish completing the cooling process. Ensure that TCS foods that have been previously cooked are cooled properly and are cooled using approved cooling methods. Foods should be cooled from 135F to 70F within a 2 hour timeframe and from 70F to 41F (or below) within 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the facility hot holding various food items in plastic containers such as but not limited to cheese sauces and gravies. Discussed with PIC that the containers are not approved to hold hot foods, nor are they sufficient enough to withstand repeat ware-washings. Instructed the facility to use stainless steel containers to hold hot foods. Ensure that materials used for hot holding are food safety approved, durable, and long lasting. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The surfaces above the drawer coolers and beneath the two flat top grills were observed with a significant amount of grease buildup. Discussed with PIC. Cleaning should occur as often as necessary to prevent buildup. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are clean and free up grease buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of the hood system above the fryers were observed with a significant amount of grease buildup. SteamPower is scheduled to service the hood system every 6 months. The last service was October 2, 2024 and the next service is scheduled for April 2, 2025. Discussed with PIC that the facility should clean the baffles in house in between scheduled SteamPower visits due to the amount of frying that occurs. The baffles are able to be placed through the dish machine or manually cleaned in the triple sink. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent grease accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: A cell phone was placed on the cutting board in the wait station area. The cell phone was removed by one of the employees. Ensure that cell phones are kept in designated places where they are not in direct contact with food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Observed stacks of cheese to be out of their original packaging and uncovered in both prep coolers along the cook-line. Discussed with PIC and cheeses were placed in a protective package. Ensure that food packaging is in good condition and that food is protected from contamination. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Observed an employee who was cutting bell peppers touch his face with a gloved hand and attempt to continue food preparation. Activity was ceased and corrected. Ensure that employees are maintaining proper handwashing, as well as protecting food from contamination. If touching of face or body occurs while preparing food, be sure to take off gloves, wash hands, and put on a fresh pair of gloves.  

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed a container of fish stored in the back standing freezer to be uncovered. The container was also broken in multiple places and small pieces of plastic were found on the fish. Discussed with PIC and fish was discarded. Ensure that fish is always covered and is stored in a manner that prevents contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the facility using soap in sani buckets to sanitize surfaces. Discussed with PIC approved sanitizing chemicals. There were bottles of bleach available in house. Fresh sani buckets were made and tested to have a 100ppm concentration (CL). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are maintained at proper concentrations in order to properly sanitize surfaces. Never add soap to sanitizer solutions. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed a cell phone placed on a cutting board in the wait station. Discussed with PIC and phone was removed. The surface was wiped down with a sani towel. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary and that phones never the surface.  

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Observed two large stock pots of cooked soup being cooled on a prep counter. PIC mentioned that soup was recently cooked and is in the process of cooling. Inspector suggested alternative methods to properly chill large batches of food. The soup was still fairly hot and was placed into shallow metal pans to speed up the cooling process. Ensure that TCS is being cooled properly. Be sure that food is being cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and from 70F to 41F or below within 4 hours. 

3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed several TCS food items being stored in prep coolers along the cook-line to not be date marked or labeled. Some items were not in their original packaging. The items include but aren’t limited to cheeses, taco meats and sauces. Items were pulled from the prep coolers and were properly labeled and date marked. Ensure that TCS foods are clearly labeled and date marked if being stored in house longer than 24 hours. Discard food items if not used within 7 days.   

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Observed two whole chickens to be thawing on the counter in the dish area. Discussed with PIC proper thawing methods and chickens were placed in the back cooler to properly thaw. PIC noted that chickens were originally thawing in a bucket that lacked running water. Ensure TCS food is being thawed using the following methods: at 41F or below under refrigeration, completely submerged under running water, or is thawed during the cooking process.   

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Observed the back standing coolers to not have hanging thermometers. Was discussed and noted in the pre-opening report. Ensure that hanging thermometers are available for every cooler to ensure proper cold holding temperatures.

4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
There wasn’t any chlorine test strips available at the facility. Facility will be purchasing test strips very soon. Ensure that test strips are available at all times to test proper sanitizing concentrations. 

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed mop head placed in a bucket in the storage area. Discussed with PIC and mop was repositioned to properly air dry. After each use, ensure that mop heads are stored in a manner that allows for them to air dry correctly.  

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
